analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
Not in the first release: previews/loans, Standard Ebooks, DIKSHA/NCERT, CORE,
HAL, Zenodo, bioRxiv/medRxiv as live sources (show "Not connected yet" if
listed), embedded readers, downloads proxied through our server, accounts.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C09 School lessons, curricula and examination resources | Education ministry portals, teacher OER networks and curriculum repositories | DIKSHA organizations, SCERTs, state boards and official examination bodies | Supported catalog/search or export; board, medium, grade and curriculum year; avoid unauthorized commercial exam copies |

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text: | [DIKSHA discovery documentation](https://diksha.gov.in/help/getting-started/explore-diksha/) | Evidence of anonymous exploration and language/location-aware search; find participating organizations | Permission or a documented stable external API merely because the website has search |

analysis_refs.heading: C09 — School lessons, curricula and examination resources
analysis_refs.text:
In India, start with [DIKSHA's discovery documentation](https://diksha.gov.in/help/getting-started/explore-diksha/),
which describes anonymous exploration and language/location filtering. Follow
the named content organizations to SCERTs, state boards and teacher-training
institutions. [NCERT's textbook portal](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) is a
lead for official textbook identities, alongside state textbook bodies and
examination-board archives. Treat textbooks shared with C04 as overlapping
category membership, not extra origins. The NCERT page returned 502 in this
review; its current retrieval route remains unverified.

analysis_refs.heading: C09 — School lessons, curricula and examination resources
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests:** investigate official catalogs, permitted exports or
attributed aggregator coverage. A DIKSHA browser endpoint is not automatically
a supported third-party API. Require item-level board, grade, medium, subject,
curriculum year and canonical resource identity where supplied. Test one lesson
in native script, a retired syllabus, a paper and its answer key, and a topic
shared across different grades. Reject unrelated or obsolete material masquerading
as the current curriculum. Preserve free enrollment versus paid examination rules.

analysis_refs.heading: Credentials and implementation inputs
analysis_refs.text: Assumptions: global discovery with explicit language/country context; lawful public hosts; verified free source login is allowed (owner clarification 2026-11-01), labelled separately from anonymous reading; no full-text hosting, subscription purchases, or library-card integration. Existing India library coverage makes NCERT, DIKSHA, StoryWeaver and Shodhganga useful follow-ups, but their discovery integrations are not assumed ready.

analysis_refs.heading: Technical recovery continuation G — 6 November 2026
analysis_refs.text:
- **NQR:** a single retry of the previously failed Mine Electrician query succeeded after roughly 90 minutes of backoff. It used the same advertised public browser form and identity. All ten current keyword cases now pass; the earlier 403 and advanced-form 500 remain saved. Availability is intermittent and no qualification files were fetched.
- **NCERT:** CIET's current ePathshala site links its actual textbook selector through a public iframe. Its published metadata contains 427 active selector rows and 421 unambiguous searchable records after repeated contexts, one unresolved subject selector and one conflicting title/native-code mapping are handled explicitly. Ten title/class searches, exact native-code and empty controls pass. Six commented metadata blocks remain inactive historical findings; no book bodies were downloaded. The footer license URL returned404, so metadata queryability does not establish reuse rights or full reading access.
- **Gallica:** BnF documents a separate public SPARQL service whose bibliographic editions link to native Gallica digital ARKs. Ten exact literal-title queries pass through that service. The parser was corrected to accept its legacy typed-literal XSD-string representation; failed attempts remain saved. Direct Gallica SRU and general-catalog restrictions are unchanged. This is a linked-data subset, not whole-Gallica keyword or full-text search.
- **SciELO:** the operator developer index and REST client document a separate anonymous ArticleMeta service. Ten native article-PID lookups now return matching Brazil-collection metadata with `body=false`. Original article title markup, language variants, journal identity, processing/publication dates and content URLs are kept separate. No article bodies were requested, and no linked content was fetched. This does not prove upstream keyword or whole-network search. The old documentation link returned404; network-search403 and regional OAI503 remain preserved.
- **Chicago zoning:** the published schema endpoint still returned503 after a multi-hour backoff. Current SODA2.1 documentation alone does not establish working dataset access. No underlying zoning query was sent after the failure.
- **OER Commons:** current operator help documents anonymous homepage search, but the primary site's policy still returns403. No homepage/search request or staging/private API workaround was sent.
- **Gutendex:** native8746 recovered after nearly two hours of backoff, but the next saved native10836 query returned503. Two of ten current native cases pass; the connector remains blocked. No broad-search retry followed that503. Unknown CLI case IDs now fail before any network dispatch, preventing silent no-op attempts.
- **DOAB and India Code:** one policy-only retry each after more than four and three hours of backoff, respectively, still timed out. No target catalog request was sent. Further timed retries are deferred until16:00UTC unless a useful recovery signal arrives.
- **DIKSHA:** the current homepage exposes14 native featured quiz links. Ten links for five topics have consistent published banner/topic/language labels and pass local metadata queries plus an empty control. Four links in two conflicting or unreviewed banner groups are quarantined. These are language variants, not extra origins. The main Library remains login-gated, and the teacher-page Search Course text is an instructional heading, not a guest search form. No course/quiz content or account flow was requested.
- **NSDC:** current public sitemap navigation revealed its sector-skills report search. Ten title-word queries and an empty-result control pass. Duplicate responsive inputs and a Search button that changes into an icon required browser-selector corrections; all failed attempts remain saved. The same operator's report-file URLs identify results without downloading PDFs. The original occupational-standards/model-curriculum catalog remains unverified and is explicitly outside this recovered subset. No staging API, direct backend replay or account flow was used.
